heading: Shared browser behavior annotations
body: Tac supports the shared behavior annotations: Setup, Needs, Named, Description, CacheSettings, Cached, UpdateCache, ClearCache, PageDefaults, Retry, MaxAtOnce, Entity, Table, Store, Query, HTTP request annotations, Settings, WhenProfile, WhenSetting, Setting, Checked, Check, Required, NotEmpty, Length, Min and Max. Every language uses these names without an import. They work in JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java and Ruby services. Lua refuses them with TY1308 (ADR 0085). A Python service writes each method that has one of these annotations with `async def` (ADR 0093). Native Swift, Kotlin, C# and Rust services, Go web services and Dart services use typed native adapters. Tac stays client-only. Validation only helps the user fill in forms (UX, the user experience). Queries call adapters (code that connects an annotation to real storage or a real network) that you choose yourself. Setup receives only TAC_ values that you made public on purpose. There is no server-side rendering (SSR), no hidden database connection, no environment snapshot and no package scanner. Native owners dispose of contexts in their own code. Synchronous adapters cannot interrupt blocking work. Setup, Entity and object-form Store declarations have roles, so they follow strict rules. Their folder names are plural, and each file name matches its type exactly. Tachyon finds them automatically in client/setups, client/entities and client/stores, next to the service. The selected sources in the same language form one metadata unit.
